definitions.explanation: A humble way to refer to one's own younger brother. An older, formal expression.
A subordinate or junior member in a hierarchical organization, especially in yakuza or gang contexts. Refers to someone who serves under a senior figure.

examples.japanese: {舎弟|しゃてい}は{今年|ことし}{大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}しました。
examples.english: My younger brother graduated from university this year.

examples.japanese: {舎弟|しゃてい}がついてまいります。
examples.english: My younger brother will accompany us.

examples.japanese: {舎弟|しゃてい}を{引|ひ}き{連|つ}れる。
{舎弟|しゃてい}たちが{兄貴|あにき}の{命令|めいれい}に{従|したが}う。
examples.english: The underlings follow the boss's orders.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{中|なか}で、{組長|くみちょう}の{舎弟|しゃてい}が{裏切|うらぎ}るシーンが{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: The scene in the movie where the boss's underling betrays him was memorable.

notes: Sense 1 is the original meaning: {舎|しゃ} is a humble prefix (as in {舎兄|しゃけい} for older brother) and {弟|てい} means younger brother. This usage is quite formal and archaic. Sense 2 is the more commonly encountered modern usage, strongly associated with yakuza films and fiction. In this context, {兄貴|あにき} (big brother/boss) and {舎弟|しゃてい} (follower/junior) form a hierarchical pair. Related: {弟|おとうと} (younger brother — standard), {兄貴|あにき} (big brother/boss), {子分|こぶん} (follower, henchman).
